item: the full-text search index after a repair cut short inside its rebuild: five test cases over real stores and a real SIGKILL name the state, and nothing assumes it
summary: Test-only (0.5.1 item 29, the FTS settle-it check): src/ and scripts/ are unchanged; the behaviour was already right and is now pinned. tests/test_repair_search_index.py, 4 test functions (5 cases) about 9 s, over the real app schema (1,300 articles, two damaged pages). (1) A stop asked inside the rebuild, noticed after it (the copy's own handler) and inside it (a finer handler of the same shape): outcome stopped, the live file byte for byte what it was, the live index still holding all 1,300 documents (read from its own shadow table) and fts_status reading the same, no scratch left, the engine never touched, the record carrying no search_index, no kept_rows, no kept_file. (2) A real child process SIGKILLed on the second batch of the rebuild: the live file untouched, one .partial copy, no sidecar, no final name; the next start plans a plain repair, counts the unfinished start, and the repaired file's index holds as many documents as the file has articles and as the report counted. (3) A cut before the swap: the sidecar's search_index.documents equals the finished copy's articles and the documents its index holds; the resume and the record carry it; the swapped-in file's index has exactly that many documents. (4) The copy's own connection interrupts a long statement once the stop it was handed is set and leaves it alone while it is clear. MEASURED: the killed copy reads clean (quick_check ok, salvage.check_copy returns (True, [])) with every article and an index of 0 documents, so only the order of the steps and the .partial name keep it from being swapped in; ensure_fts at boot heals only a fully empty index, never a partial one; fts_status CANNOT SEE the index: over an index emptied with delete-all it reads healthy with rows equal to the articles (an external-content table is read through its content table), so the tests read article_fts_docsize; the copy's stop poll (100,000 steps of one statement) did not notice a stop inside a 4,000-document rebuild and interrupted 8,000, 12,000 and 16,000 article rebuilds after 15 batches (7,500 documents). Field storage-events.json carries six kinds and no repair or index kind, so the field data neither shows nor contradicts a case. RED WITHOUT: rebuild never run, search_index not carried by the sidecar, rebuild stopping after its first batch, a stop not honoured once the copy is back, an interrupted rebuild read as a failure, the next start not removing the killed copy, an index that counts its batches and indexes nothing, a copy not handed the repair's stop and a copy connection with no progress handler are all red; the interrupted-to-stopped mapping alone, shadowed by the check before it, stays green and is named. Three proposals, not made: fts_status reports the index's own document count (recommendation: yes, in fts.py when it is free), poll the cancel flag between batches (no), compare the documents with the copy's article count before the sidecar (no for now).
